facts.text: The hotel is a former 16th-century baroque monastery.
facts.excerpt: Our luxury hotel in Cusco is a former 16th-century baroque monastery, home to the powerful art and architecture of the Cusco School.

facts.text: The hotel rests on the original foundations of Inca Emperor Amaru Qhata's palace.
facts.excerpt: Resting on the original foundations of Inca Emperor Amaru Qhata

facts.text: In 1595 the site became the San Antonio Abad Monastery.
facts.excerpt: In 1595, the site was transformed into the San Antonio Abad Monastery, a place of devotion and study for generations of monks.

facts.text: The hotel opened as a luxury hotel in 1965.
facts.excerpt: Centuries later, in 1965, Monasterio entered a new era as a luxury hotel

facts.text: The courtyards are gathered around a 300-year-old Andean cedar.
facts.excerpt: its serene courtyards gathered around a 300-year-old Andean cedar

facts.text: Oqre serves Peruvian cuisine with a twist.
facts.excerpt: Peruvian with a twist at Oqre

facts.text: El Tupay serves international fine dining.
facts.excerpt: International fine dining at El Tupay

facts.text: Guests can dine under stone arches to the sound of live opera in El Tupay.
facts.excerpt: under romantic stone arches to the sound of live opera in El Tupay

facts.text: The hotel has a collection of prized Cusco School art.
facts.excerpt: Collection of prized Cusco School art

facts.text: The hotel has an ornate baroque chapel.
The hotel has a spa treatment suite.

facts.text: The hotel is a 3.5 hour train ride from Machu Picchu.
